MUQATIL:18:25-26/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:25-26/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:25-26/r3.claim: Muhammad is told to answer the Christians of Najran that God knows best how long they remained asleep.

MUQATIL:18:25-26/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:25-26/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:25-26/r4.claim: God knows the unseen of the heavens and earth, including what will occur in them; none sees or hears better than He.

MUQATIL:18:25-26/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:25-26/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:25-26/r5.claim: They have no protector besides God who can benefit them, and He shares His judgment with nobody.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p180#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p180#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p180#2/r1.claim: Qatāda says God answers the claimed duration by declaring Himself the knower of how long they stayed and of the unseen in heaven and earth.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p180#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p180#2/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p180#2/r2.claim: The phrase 'How seeing and hearing He is!' is an Arabic expression like saying that someone is exceedingly discerning; Qatāda says no one sees or hears more than God.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p180#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p180#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p180#2/r3.claim: No protector besides God can shield people from His punishment.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p180#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p180#2/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p180#2/r4.claim: Two readings are reported: address the Prophet not to associate anyone in judgment, or state that God shares His judgment with no one.

FARRA:v2p138/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p138/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p138/r6.claim: أبصر به وأسمع is an exclamation meaning how seeing and hearing He is; the same form expresses praise or blame, retaining doubled consonants and weak letters.

FARRA:v2p138/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p138/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p138/r7.claim: The doubled form stays undivided because the exclamatory verb cannot be dualized or pluralized; مد is an exception because ordinary forms مدا and مدوا exist.

FARRA:v2p139/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p139/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p139/r1.claim: ولا يشرك with ياء is indicative, meaning He does not share; لا تشرك with تاء is a jussive prohibition.

AKHFASH:v2p429#2/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p429#2/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p429#2/r3.claim: أبصر به وأسمع is an exclamation meaning How perceptive and hearing He is!, like أكرم به; a command would instead be أكرمي زيدا.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#3/r1.claim: Although the preceding verse gave their stay as three hundred years plus nine, this says God knows best because people disputed its duration.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#3/r2.claim: Abṣir bihi wa-asmiʿ is an exclamation: how seeing and hearing He is!

TAB-FULL:v15p231/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī holds that God states their actual stay: three hundred years and nine from entering the cave until He awakened and exposed them; the verse gives this directly.

TAB-FULL:v15p231/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r4.claim: He rejects treating 18:25 as an unmarked quotation of the People of the Book: the text gives no signal of reported speech, and a claim about God’s words needs proof.

TAB-FULL:v15p231/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r5.claim: He reads God knows best how long they remained as referring to the time after their souls were taken following their awakening, up to the revelation; only God or one informed by Him knows it.

TAB-FULL:v15p233/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p233/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p233/r1.claim: God knows the unseen of heaven and earth without anything escaping or being hidden from Him, so people should leave to Him the unknown duration after the youths’ awakening.

TAB-FULL:v15p234#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p234#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p234#2/r1.claim: Creatures have no protector apart from their Lord to manage their affairs; God alone decides and governs them, without a partner in judgment.

TAB-FULL:v15p234/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p234/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p234/r1.claim: أبصر به وأسمع is emphatic praise: God sees every existing thing and hears every sound, with nothing hidden from His sight or hearing.

TAB-FULL:v15p234/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p234/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p234/r2.claim: Qatāda says no one sees or hears better than God.

TAB-FULL:v15p234/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p234/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p234/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says God sees people’s deeds and hears them.

ZAJJAJ:v3p279/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p279/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p279/r1.claim: Scholars agree أبصر به وأسمع means how perfectly seeing and hearing He is; God knows the Cave companions' story.

ZAJJAJ:v3p279/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p279/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p279/r2.claim: ولا يشرك may be read as prohibition; تشرك may address the listener and prohibit ascribing unseen knowledge to anyone.

ZAJJAJ:v3p279/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p279/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p279/r3.claim: The third-person reading means God shares His unseen with no one, as stated in the verse about revealing the unseen.

ZAJJAJ:v3p279/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p279/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p279/r4.claim: A strong legal reading forbids judges from deciding except by God's rule or its indication, lest they share authority to prescribe law.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r2.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir alone reads ولا تشرك with tāʾ and jazm; all others read ولا يشرك with yāʾ and رفع.

NAHHAS:v2p453/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p453/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p453/r9.claim: ‘How seeing and hearing He is’ has imperative form with inflection omitted, but functions as an exclamation: how well He hears and sees.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223/r4.claim: The yāʾ with indicative رفع reports God's action and makes لا mean ليس; tāʾ with jazm addresses the Messenger and makes لا prohibitive.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p141#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p141#2/r1.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p141#2/r1.claim: All readers except Ibn ʿĀmir read the third-person indicative يَشْرِكُ, continuing the preceding references to an absent subject; God does not share His judgment with anyone.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p141#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p141#2/r2.speaker: ابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p141#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads the second-person jussive prohibition, addressing a person: do not associate anyone in God's judgment.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p141#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p141#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p141#2/r3.claim: The third-person reading is more widespread; the shift from divine absence to direct address is also idiomatic, as in the change to إياك نعبد.

THALABI:v6p165/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p165/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p165/r3.claim: The expressions about seeing and hearing mean that God sees every existing thing and hears every audible thing.

THALABI:v6p165/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p165/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p165/r4.claim: No one besides God is a guardian or helper for the inhabitants of heaven and earth.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r10.claim: Alternatively, ولي may mean a protector or someone able to prevent harm.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r11.claim: God shares His judgment with no one because no one shares His knowledge of the unseen.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r12.claim: Alternatively, He gave no one authority to judge contrary to His judgment, so no one can share His rule.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r5.claim: Allah knows how long they remained after their period of sleep up to the revelation of the Quran about them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r6.claim: Alternatively, Allah knows how long they stayed in the cave, the period for which the Jews gave a figure that included an addition or subtraction.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r7.claim: أبصر به وأسمع may praise God as seeing what people say and hearing what they say.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r8.claim: Alternatively, it means that God shows them and makes them hear what He has said about them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r9.claim: ولي may mean a helper or supporter.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p593/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p593/r1.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p593/r1.claim: “How perfectly He sees and hears!” is an exclamation, like “How generous Zayd is!”; if it were a command to a woman, it would take a different form.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p593/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p593/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p593/r2.claim: The referent is God: the construction means “How generous Abdullah is”; “how well they hear and see” in Maryam means the same kind of exclamation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p593/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p593/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p593/r3.claim: Scholars agree that the phrase means “How well He hears and sees,” showing His knowledge of the Cave Companions and others.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p593/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p593/r4.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p593/r4.claim: Arabic can use an imperative-shaped exclamation as a report and a report-shaped phrase as a prayer; the preposition and noun together occupy nominative position.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p595/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p595/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p595/r1.claim: The imperative-shaped expression has become a conventional exclamation, with no difference in meaning from “How excellent Zayd is!”

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p595/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p595/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p595/r2.claim: The phrase means that God sees every existent and hears every audible thing; al-Wahidi says scholars agree on this exclamatory reading.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p595/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p595/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p595/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd explains that God sees the deeds of those in the heavens and earth and hears them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p595/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p595/r4.speaker: ابن عباس رواية عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p595/r4.claim: A minority reading takes this as a command: make God's friends see the Quran's marvels and hear through it; the object is omitted, but al-Wahidi says the established view is the exclamation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p596/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p596/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p596/r1.claim: “They have no guardian besides Him” means the inhabitants of the heavens and earth have no protector besides God; the pronoun returns to those inhabitants mentioned in the preceding phrase.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p596/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p596/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p596/r2.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers specifically to believers: having recognized God's majesty and lordship, they take no guardian besides Him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p596/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p596/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p596/r3.claim: “No one shares His judgment” can mean no one shares God's knowledge and power concerning the unseen, as in the Jinn verse, or that no judge may rule except by God's rulings and evidence from them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p596/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p596/r4.speaker: ابن عامر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p596/r4.claim: Ibn Amir reads “do not associate” as a prohibition addressed to a human against making anyone share God's judgment; it shifts from third person to direct address and echoes the idols verse.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p596/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p596/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p596/r5.claim: The common “He does not associate” reading fits better because the preceding clause has God as the absent third-person referent.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r1.claim: God knows best how long the youths remained; he knows everything hidden in the heavens and earth, sees every existent, and hears every sound.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r2.claim: There is no protector besides God and no one can share his judgment or issue a ruling he has not made.

JISHUMI:v6p4386/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4386/r2.speaker: ابن عامر ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v6p4386/r2.claim: They read ولا تشرك with a second-person prohibition; the other readers use the indicative, saying that God has no partner in judgment.

JISHUMI:v6p4392/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r10.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r10.claim: He says God knows how long they remained until the Qurʾān's revelation, or until they died, or simply knows without having told them.

JISHUMI:v6p4392/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r11.claim: God alone knows the unseen of the heavens and earth; ‘how seeing and hearing He is’ is an expression of wonder and exaltation, like the Arabic praise ‘how generous Zayd is.’

JISHUMI:v6p4392/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r12.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r12.claim: An alternative takes the phrase as a command to proclaim this to people, since God is hearing and seeing.

JISHUMI:v6p4392/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r13.claim: The pronoun in ‘they have no protector’ may refer to the cave youths, but the better reading is all people, who have no protector besides God.

JISHUMI:v6p4392/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r14.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r14.claim: ‘No one shares His judgment’ may mean He needs no assistant, no one possesses judgment with Him, no one shares in His creation and beneficence, or idols have no divinity.

JISHUMI:v6p4395/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4395/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4395/r4.claim: The description ‘how seeing and hearing He is’ affirms God's hearing and sight of secret and public, near and far, without imperfection.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165#2/r1.speaker: علي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165#2/r1.claim: Ali explains the extra nine as the difference between three hundred solar years known to the People of the Book and three hundred lunar years in the Qur'an: three years per century.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165#2/r2.claim: The unseen is whatever escapes perception, but nothing escapes God's perception.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165#2/r3.claim: The exclamation says how fully God sees every existent thing and hears every audible thing.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165#2/r4.speaker: ابن عامر ويعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165#2/r4.claim: They read the closing verb as a direct prohibition: do not associate anyone in judgment.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165#2/r5.claim: The other reading says God associates no one in His judgment; judgment here may mean knowledge of the unseen.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r10.claim: The pronoun in “they have” refers to the inhabitants of the heavens and earth; a wali is one who manages their affairs.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r11.claim: No one shares God’s judgment or decree.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r12.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r12.claim: Al-Hasan reads the phrase as a prohibition addressed to the listener: “do not associate.”

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r2.claim: “Say: God knows best” means God knows their duration better than those disputing it; the truth is what He revealed to the Prophet.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r3.claim: Qatada says the statement quotes the People of the Book, and “God knows best” answers them.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r9.claim: God alone knows what is hidden in the heavens and earth; the expressions of seeing and hearing marvelously signal perception beyond human limits, of the tiniest and largest, hidden and visible.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r2.claim: Qatada takes 'how seeing and hearing He is' as an exclamation: no one sees or hears more fully than God.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r3.claim: Alternatively, God sees by His revelation and guidance and lets the Prophet see proofs and truth; the two verbs may express two distinct ideas rather than an exclamation.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r4.claim: The pronoun in 'they have no protector' may refer to the sleepers, whom no one besides God guarded, or to the Prophet's unbelieving opponents, as a threat.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r5.claim: Most readers use the indicative 'and He does not associate anyone in His judgment'; Ibn Amir, al-Hasan, Abu Raja, Qatada, and al-Jahdari read it as a prohibition addressed to the Prophet, while Mujahid has a jussive reading whose grammar Yaqub cannot explain.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r7.claim: On a Syrian campaign Ibn Abbas saw bones at a cave and said the sleepers had perished long ago; a monk was surprised that an Arab knew this.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r8.claim: Another tradition says the Prophet foretold that Jesus would make the pilgrimage with the sleepers, who had not yet made it.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p511/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p511/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p511/r1.claim: Many people in Syria identify a cave with corpses, a mosque, a structure called al-Raqim, and a dog skeleton as the sleepers' site; Ibn Atiyya says he also visited the reported cave near Loja in Granada in 504 AH and saw corpses and a dog remains, nearby Roman ruins and a site called Daqiyus.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p511/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p511/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p511/r2.claim: He records these claimed sites because their enduring marvel is worth remembering, though earlier generations left no reliable indication of their identity.

TABRISI:18:25-26/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:25-26/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:25-26/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, Rawḥ, Zayd from Yaʿqūb, and Sahl read ولا تشرك with second-person tāʾ in the jussive; the others read ولا يشرك with third-person yāʾ and indicative.

TABRISI:18:25-26/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:25-26/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:25-26/r6.claim: The third-person reading is more widespread and preferable because the preceding context uses third-person forms; its meaning is that no one shares God's judgment.

TABRISI:18:25-27/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:25-27/r1.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:18:25-27/r1.claim: Qatada says the three-hundred-year statement is a quotation from the Jews, reasoning from the following instruction to say that God knows how long they stayed.

TABRISI:18:25-27/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:25-27/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:25-27/r2.claim: The author rejects treating God's statement as a quotation without decisive evidence; that reading leaves their duration unstated and defeats the passage's proof of God's power.

TABRISI:18:25-27/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:25-27/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:25-27/r3.claim: The duration has already been given; ‘God knows best’ refutes scripture scholars' disagreement, directing them to God's report rather than their own estimates.

TABRISI:18:25-27/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:25-27/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:25-27/r4.claim: The unseen is what lies beyond perception; nothing in the heavens or earth is hidden from God's knowledge, including what creatures cannot perceive.

TABRISI:18:25-27/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:25-27/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:25-27/r5.claim: ‘How perfectly He sees and hears’ is an exclamation of exaltation: God perceives every visible thing and hears every sound.

TABRISI:18:25-27/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:25-27/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:25-27/r6.claim: A Jew asked Ali about the youths' duration; Ali answered that the Qur'anic nine years reconcile the difference between lunar years and the solar years in their scripture.

TABRISI:18:25-27/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:25-27/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:25-27/r7.claim: No one in heaven or earth can protect or support creatures independently of God.

TABRISI:18:25-27/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:25-27/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:25-27/r8.claim: On ولا يشرك, one reading means no judge may rule contrary to God's judgment; the alternative imperative means not to associate anyone with God in judgment, while another gloss limits the sense to God's unique knowledge of the unseen.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r1.claim: God knows the duration better than the disputing People of the Book.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r2.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r2.claim: Christians of Najran said they understood the three hundred years but had no knowledge of the additional nine; the verse then affirmed that God knows best.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r3.claim: Another account says the People of the Book counted 309 years from the youths' entry into the cave until their own time, whereas the verse refers to the time after their souls were taken, known only to God.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r4.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r4.claim: The nine years account for the difference between solar and lunar years.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r5.claim: أبصر به وأسمع is an exclamation: how perfectly God sees and hears; He knows the Cave story and all else, a reading he says scholars unanimously accept.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r6.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is an imperative to see and hear God's religion or guidance; the pronoun refers to God or guidance.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r7.claim: No one can protect the inhabitants of heaven and earth besides God, or independently judge contrary to His ruling and thereby share His judgment.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r8.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p131/r8.claim: He reads ولا تشرك with jussive tāʾ, an address commanding the human not to associate partners with God.

RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r10.claim: The other readers use third-person yaʾ with indicative mood, stating that God does not share His judgment.

RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r5.claim: God knows the duration better than disputing people because He created the heavens and earth and governs the world, so He necessarily knows its unseen events.

RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r6.claim: “How seeing and hearing He is” is an Arabic expression of wonder, discussed also in the commentary on 2:175.

RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r7.claim: “They have no protector besides Him” may mean God alone preserved the sleepers; that disputants need His care and cannot know without His informing them; or that no protector can shield those who defy His report from punishment.

RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r8.claim: No one shares God's judgment: a partner could object and impede the other, as in the argument that multiple gods would bring disorder.

RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r9.speaker: ابن عامر
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r9.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads lā tushrik with second-person tāʾ and jussive, attaching the prohibition to “do not say” or “remember your Lord”; it means do not consult anyone about their number or seek another's knowledge.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:26#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26#2/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya cites a report that Jesus will perform pilgrimage with the Cave Companions, who have not yet made pilgrimage.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:26#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26#2/r2.claim: On this account, the youths remain asleep rather than dead until shortly before the Hour; the author says scripture identifies Jesus as God’s servant and messenger and says he will pass al-Rawha as pilgrim or visitor.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r1.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r1.claim: Mujahid takes the stated duration as the time from the youths’ death until the Qur’an revealed their story.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r10.claim: The ya reading with a nominative kaf reports that God shares His judgment with none.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r11.speaker: ابن عامر والحسن وأبو رجاء وقتادة والجحدري
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r11.claim: These readers use second-person ta with a still kaf, addressing the Prophet and coordinating the clause with the command to see and hear.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r12.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r12.claim: Mujahid reads the ya with a jussive; Yaqub says he does not know its grammatical basis.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas said the youths had perished: near their cave he found bones and told his party they had vanished long ago.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r2.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says the duration means until the youths died.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r3.claim: Another reported interpretation measures their time in the cave, the duration Jews had given with additions and omissions.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r4.claim: Only God knows the duration, unless He has disclosed it to someone.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r5.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r5.claim: Qatadah reads the phrase as an exclamation: none sees or hears better than God; the wording describes perception.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r6.claim: An alternative takes the verbs as commands: by His revelation and guidance God showed the Prophet the truth and made the world hear it.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r7.claim: Another reading means that God showed the youths and made them hear what He said about them.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r8.claim: The lack of any guardian may refer to the Cave Companions, whom only God protected.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:26/r9.claim: Alternatively it refers to disbelievers disputing the youths’ duration: they have no manager besides God, so cannot know without His disclosure.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:26/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:26/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:26/r1.claim: God knows all hidden conditions of the heavens and earth; nothing among their inhabitants escapes His knowledge.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:26/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:26/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:26/r2.claim: The exclamation about God's seeing and hearing stresses perception beyond created senses: nothing veils Him and subtle, dense, small, great, hidden, and clear are alike to Him.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:26/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:26/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:26/r3.claim: Sibawayh parses the pronoun as nominative and the preposition as extra; al-Akhfash instead parses the pronoun as object and the doer as an implied command addressed to everyone.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:26/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:26/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:26/r4.claim: God alone governs all beings, with no protector for them and no one sharing His judgment.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:26/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:26/r5.speaker: ابن عامر وقالون عن يعقوب
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:26/r5.claim: Ibn Amir and Qalun from Yaqub read the final verb as a jussive prohibition in the second person against anyone associating in judgment.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:26/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:26/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:26/r6.claim: The unseen story of the sleepers proves revelation to the Prophet; he is then commanded to continue reciting the Book and keep company with its people.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#2/r1.claim: “God knows best how long” may be God's correction of those disputing about the sleepers, or the People of the Book's statement repeated as a rebuttal.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#2/r2.claim: The majority holds that God states they remained in the cave for the duration He has reported.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#2/r3.claim: God alone knows hidden conditions of the inhabitants of heaven and earth; no one besides Him governs them, and none shares in His judgment.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#2/r4.claim: The emphatic expressions mean how perfectly God sees every existent and hears every audible thing.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11#2/r5.claim: The Syrian reading makes “do not associate anyone” a prohibition; the context answers demands to bring a different Qur'an or alter it.

QASHANI:18:25-26/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:25-26/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:25-26/r3.claim: The years remain indefinite in the wording; this supports the statement that God knows best how long they stayed.

QASHANI:18:25-26/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:25-26/r4.speaker: قتادة
QASHANI:18:25-26/r4.claim: Qatada says the duration is a continuation of the People of the Book’s reported claim, which the command that God knows best rejects.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r5.claim: After giving the exact duration, God commands the Prophet to say that God knows best: this is certain truth because God knows the unseen of heaven and earth.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r6.claim: ما لبثوا may refer to the preceding sleep, or to the time from their discovery until the Prophet’s era.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r1.claim: One view says the Prophet is told to return knowledge of the duration to God, refuting others; Abū Ḥayyān prefers that the phrase belongs to the disputants, as the context indicates and because the matter is among God’s hidden knowledge.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r10.claim: The pronoun in به refers to God; grammarians disagree whether the expression is nominative or accusative and whether the verbs are literal commands or formulas of amazement.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r11.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya, citing Ibn al-Anbārī, allows ‘see by God’s religion and hear by His guidance,’ with the pronoun referring to guidance or God.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r12.speaker: عيسى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r12.claim: ʿĪsā reads أسمع به وأبصر as past indicatives, meaning God made His servants perceive Him through knowledge and made them hear; the pronoun refers to God.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r9.claim: God knows all unseen affairs in the heavens and earth; أبصر به وأسمع expresses the extraordinary reach of His perception, from the smallest and hidden things to the largest and most visible.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p165/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p165/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p165/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes ما لهم to refer to the inhabitants of heaven and earth, who have no independent guardian over their affairs.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p165/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p165/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p165/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya offers several possible referents for ما لهم: the cave youths, the Prophet’s hostile contemporaries as a threat, believers in heaven and earth, or those disputing the youths’ duration, who cannot know without God’s disclosure.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p165/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p165/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p165/r3.claim: Most readers have ولا يشرك in the indicative with yāʾ, stating that no one shares God’s judgment.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p165/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p165/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p165/r4.claim: Mujāhid reads ولا يشرك with yāʾ in the jussive; Yaʿqūb says he does not know the rationale.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p165/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p165/r5.speaker: ابن عامر والحسن وأبو رجاء وقتادة والجحدري وأبو حيوة وزيد وحميد بن الوزير والجعفي واللؤلؤي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p165/r5.claim: This group reads ولا تشرك with second-person tāʾ and jussive as a prohibition.

SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r1.claim: أبصر به is a metaphorical exclamation meaning ما أبصره, with the pronoun referring to God.

SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r10.speaker: مجاهد
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r10.claim: Mujahid also reads the verb with second-person ta and jussive mood.

SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r11.speaker: يعقوب
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r11.claim: Yaqub says he cannot identify the grammatical basis for Mujahid's reading.

SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r12.claim: The author supplies the basis: the subject is an understood human pronoun, omitted because it is known.

SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r13.claim: The pronoun in مالهم refers to the contemporaries of the Messenger.

SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r14.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r14.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls the verse an interrupting threat, meaning it concerns people beyond those previously addressed, not a technical parenthesis.

SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r2.claim: The strongest analysis treats the form as an imperative in wording but declarative in meaning, with an extra ب before the grammatical subject.

SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r3.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r3.claim: A second analysis makes the grammatical subject a pronoun referring to the verbal noun.

SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r4.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r4.claim: A third analysis takes the subject as the addressee: the command means that the addressee sees.

SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r5.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r5.claim: Another view takes it as a literal command rather than an exclamation and refers the pronoun to guidance understood from context.

SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r6.speaker: عيسى
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r6.claim: Isa read أبصر and أسمع as past verbs with God as subject; به likewise refers to God, who made His servants see and hear.

SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r7.claim: من ولي may be parsed either as a grammatical subject or as a topic.

SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r8.speaker: ابن عامر
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r8.claim: Ibn Amir reads ولا تشرك in second person with a jussive verb, addressing the human listener.

SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r9.speaker: الباقون
SAMIN-DURR:18:26/r9.claim: The other readers use third-person ي and an indicative verb, a straightforward denial that anyone shares God's judgment.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150#2/r2.claim: Without revealed knowledge or instruction about their duration, one must not speculate but say God knows; only God, or someone He informs, knows the unseen. Ibn Kathir says this is also the view of many early and later exegetes, including Mujahid.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150#2/r3.claim: Qatada, followed by Mutarrif ibn Abd Allah, says the three hundred years plus nine was the People of the Book's statement, rejected by the following command to say God knows; he cites a variant reading attributed to Ibn Masud, وقالوا ولبثوا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects Qatada's attribution: the People of the Book give three hundred solar years without nine; the verse is God's own report, as Ibn Jarir also chose. The Ibn Masud reading has a disconnected transmission and is anomalous against the majority reading, so it is not evidence.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151/r1.claim: The phrase means God sees and hears them. Ibn Jarir treats it as emphatic praise: God sees every existing thing and hears every audible thing, with nothing hidden from Him.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151/r2.claim: Qatada says no one sees more clearly or hears better than God.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says God sees people's deeds and hears them, being all-hearing and all-seeing.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p151/r4.claim: God alone possesses creation and command; no one can overturn His judgment, and He has no minister, helper, partner, or adviser.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p461/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p461/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p461/r3.claim: God alone knows the sleepers' duration because He comprehends all unseen things, never forgets, and cannot be thwarted in what is to come.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p461/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p461/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p461/r4.claim: The expressions of seeing and hearing proclaim that God's perception is perfect beyond human comprehension and is the basis of knowledge.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r1.claim: No guardian can shield anyone from God or replace His report; no one shares in His judgment or can report independently of His command.

DURR-FULL:v5p379/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says 309 years is what people reported, not God's own assertion; otherwise God would not have said that He knows best how long they remained.

DURR-FULL:v5p379/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r2.claim: The Ibn Masud reading says people reported the 300 years; Qatada cites God's command to say that He knows best as confirmation.

DURR-FULL:v5p379/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r3.claim: Qatada says the 300 years and nine is the People of the Book's statement, which God answers by saying He knows best.

DURR-FULL:v5p379/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says God is the one who says “How seeing and hearing He is.”

DURR-FULL:v5p379/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r7.claim: No one sees or hears more fully than God, exalted is He.

BURSEVI:v5p182#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p182#2/r1.speaker: البغوي
BURSEVI:v5p182#2/r1.claim: If people dispute the duration, he says to answer that God knows the time spent, since knowledge of the hidden belongs to Him.

BURSEVI:v5p182#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p182#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p182#2/r2.claim: God alone knows what is hidden from earth's inhabitants; the exclamation describes how perfectly He sees every existent and hears every audible thing.

BURSEVI:v5p182#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p182#2/r3.speaker: الشيخ
BURSEVI:v5p182#2/r3.claim: He parses the pronoun after أبصر and أسمع as the subject of an exclamatory verb, with extra bāʾ; the form is not a command, and the exclamation is figurative since astonishment is impossible for God.

BURSEVI:v5p182#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p182#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p182#2/r4.claim: God's perception exceeds created perception: nothing blocks it, and fine, coarse, small, great, hidden, and manifest are equal to Him; sight precedes hearing because the subject is visible things.

BURSEVI:v5p182#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p182#2/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p182#2/r5.claim: God sees every existent and hears every audible thing, and it is through Him that people see and hear.

BURSEVI:v5p182#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p182#2/r6.speaker: القيصري
BURSEVI:v5p182#2/r6.claim: He describes divine hearing as disclosure through knowledge of essential speech, seeing as knowing realities through witnessing, and speech as disclosure through will and power that brings the unseen into existence.

BURSEVI:v5p182#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p182#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p182#2/r7.claim: The inhabitants of heaven and earth have no independently governing ally; God gives no being a share in His eternal decree because of His majesty and self-sufficiency.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#3/r1.claim: The command to say that God knows best confirms the period already given as the true duration of their sleep; delaying the clarification signals disagreement over duration and marks this hidden report as a prophetic miracle, echoing the earlier conclusion about their number.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r1.claim: The forms “How seeing and hearing!” are exclamations spoken within the commanded recitation, not an expression of divine surprise; creatures may truly marvel at God's attributes and acts, as a hadith illustrates.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r2.claim: The phrasing indicates that God's sight and hearing are attributes distinct from knowledge: the subtle and gross, small and great, hidden and open are equally unobstructed.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r3.claim: Some say existing and nonexistent things are alike in relation to divine sight and hearing, based on the debated thesis that nonexistent things have thingness.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r4.claim: Sībawayh parses the forms as originally “became seeing” and “became hearing,” then recast into imperative-shaped exclamations with an explicit subject marked by an extra preposition; the phrase carries a nominative subject and genitive surface form.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r5.speaker: الرضي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r5.claim: Al-Raḍī objects that Sībawayh's past-tense analysis is unattested and that becoming an attribute is rare, while the added preposition is usual with objects, not subjects.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī replies that imperative forms can carry a past-like sense, citing al-Zajjāj's explanation of “enough by him” as “take satisfaction in him”; the performative exclamation is also more natural in an imperative shape.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r7.speaker: الأخفش
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers the analysis attributed to al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ: the form is an imperative to everyone to describe God as seeing and hearing, a reading that suits exclamation better than Sībawayh's account.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254#2/r8.claim: On this analysis the subject is an unspecified addressee, the form is fixed because it has become an idiom of exclamation, and the added preposition marks the object; al-Zajjāj's alternative makes the hamza causative but is strained.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r7.claim: God's unseen encompasses everything hidden in the heavens and earth; because He knows what is hidden, He necessarily knows all other created things as well.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p255/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p255/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p255/r1.claim: The analyses differ if the preposition is omitted under necessity: Sībawayh's account requires the governed noun to become nominative, while the imperative analysis requires accusative.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p255/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p255/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v15p255/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya suggests “see by God's religion and hear by it,” with the pronoun referring to guidance or to God; al-Ālūsī rejects this interpretation.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p255/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p255/r3.speaker: عيسى
ALUSI-FULL:v15p255/r3.claim: ʿĪsā reads both verbs as past tense; Abū Ḥayyān takes the wording as a report rather than an exclamation, meaning God enabled His servants to see and hear through knowledge of Him.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p255/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p255/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p255/r4.claim: Another possibility takes both forms as comparatives used circumstantially of God, with the pronoun referring to the unseen; it denotes perfect sight and hearing rather than literal comparison, and al-Ālūsī finds it closer than Abū Ḥayyān's reading.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p255/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p255/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p255/r5.claim: “They have no guardian besides Him” refers generally to the inhabitants of the heavens and earth, whose affairs God alone governs.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p255/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p255/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v15p255/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya offers several possible referents for “they”: the cave youths, the Prophet's hostile contemporaries, believing people of heaven and earth, or those disputing the sleepers' duration; al-Ālūsī calls these readings weak.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p255/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p255/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p255/r7.claim: The wording “no guardian … and no one shares His judgment” more forcefully denies a partner than a simpler statement that there is no partner.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p256/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p256/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p256/r1.claim: Mujāhid reads the verb with yāʾ and jussive ending; Yaʿqūb says he knows no basis, while others explain the form as a pause-like sukūn.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p256/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p256/r2.speaker: ابن عامر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p256/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ, Qatāda, and others read with tāʾ and a jussive, as a prohibition against shirk addressed to everyone; if directed to the Prophet it would indirectly admonish others, like the quoted poetic address.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p256/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p256/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p256/r3.claim: The tāʾ reading could address the Prophet and connect to the earlier command not to make a definite promise, meaning to ask no one about the cave story or its duration and rely on revelation; al-Ālūsī finds this far from the apparent construction.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r10.claim: The exclamation means that God's sight and hearing are incomparable; on a monistic reading His attributes are identical with His essence.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r11.claim: No one is a protector besides God because no one acts independently of Him, and He shares His judgment with no one because His power is perfect and others are incapable.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r7.claim: The hidden of the heavens and earth means the upper and lower worlds; hiddenness is only relative to creatures, since nothing is unseen to God.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r8.claim: Some say God does not know the unseen because nothing is unseen to Him; al-Ālūsī says such wording must not be used, even with that intended interpretation, because it appears to contradict Quranic verses.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r9.claim: Al-Ālūsī condemns people who obscure truth through riddles and thereby mislead others.

ELMALILI:18:24-26/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:18:24-26/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:18:24-26/r10.claim: The companions have no patron apart from God and are not among those who claim He has a son; no one shares in God's judgment.

ELMALILI:18:24-26/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:18:24-26/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:18:24-26/r9.claim: If people dispute how long they stayed, answer that God knows best, as the sleepers themselves said; He owns heaven and earth's unseen and sees and hears perfectly.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r1.claim: If 18:25 is God’s own duration report, 18:26 ends disputes among the People of the Book; if it quotes them, the Prophet is told to defer knowledge to God as at 18:22.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r2.claim: The unseen of heavens and earth includes all entities and conditions hidden from people; the fronted ‘to Him’ restricts this knowledge to God, against claims to know the sleepers’ history.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r3.claim: The paired exclamations marvel at God’s comprehensive knowledge of unseen sights and sounds, which no one shares.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r4.claim: The denial that they have any guardian besides Him invalidates the polytheists’ claimed divine protectors through a general negative construction.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r5.claim: The denial of partners in God’s judgment rebuts their claim that their idols share His sovereignty.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r6.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r6.claim: Most readers use third-person indicative yushriku, whose pronoun returns to God in the preceding phrase.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r7.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads the verb in second person and jussive after prohibitive lā, addressing the Prophet, his community, or any listener.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301#2/r8.claim: Ibn Ashur closes the sleepers’ story here and remarks that exegetes have transmitted many fabricated reports about it.

TABATABAI:18:26#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:26#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:26#2/r1.claim: The pronoun in to them most plausibly refers to the Cave youths, though it could refer to rational beings or everyone in heaven and earth.

TABATABAI:18:26#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:26#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:26#2/r2.claim: The verse gives a general proof that God knows their duration because He owns and perceives all unseen things, plus a specific proof because He alone directly governs them.

TABATABAI:18:26#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:26#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:26#2/r3.claim: The two causal proof clauses are detached rather than conjoined because each explains why God knows their duration.

TABATABAI:18:26#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:26#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:26#3/r3.claim: A report’s claim that the duration in 18:25 is the People of the Book’s statement rejected by 18:26 is incompatible with the surrounding passage and its eloquent structure.

TABATABAI:18:26#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:26#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:26#4/r1.claim: Reports differ over whether the youths died or slept again and whether the three hundred and nine years came from God or the People of the Book; the broadly shared account is that monotheists fled a coercive polytheist king and slept in a cave.

TABATABAI:18:26/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:26/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:26/r1.claim: God’s greater knowledge is asserted because people disputed the duration; His ownership of the unseen in heaven and earth means nothing escapes Him.

TABATABAI:18:26/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:26/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:26/r2.claim: The phrase He is most seeing and hearing is an exclamatory expression of perfect perception, completing the argument for His knowledge rather than repeating it.

TABATABAI:18:26/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:26/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:26/r3.claim: The lam means exclusive ownership, not merely possession of knowledge; the alternative makes the seeing-and-hearing phrase redundant and wrongly implies other beings know all the unseen.

TABATABAI:18:26/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:26/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:26/r4.claim: The first clause denies another guardian with independent authority; the following clause denies any partner in God’s judgment, including delegated administration or adjudication.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.claim: The cave story circulated in detailed reports from al-Qummī, Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, Mujāhid, Ibn Isḥāq, Wahb ibn Munabbih, and al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr, among others.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.claim: The transmitted accounts disagree even on major features, while reports about dates, rulers, lineage, appearance, names, and the title أصحاب الرقيم diverge still more.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.claim: One cause is the story’s prominence among People of the Book: Quraysh learned it from them, and its Christian images and monuments spread it widely, so communities reshaped it to fit their beliefs.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.claim: A second cause is Muslims’ broad collection of outside reports, especially through converts such as Wahb ibn Munabbih and Kaʿb al-Aḥbār; later transmitters treated such material as prophetic reports.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.claim: The Qurʾān selects key lessons that serve guidance instead of supplying a complete historical account; it is a book of guidance, not history.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r1.claim: The Qurʾān omits names, ancestry, birth, upbringing, occupations, social standing, dates, rulers, cities, persecutors, and the dog’s identity because guidance does not depend on them; historians and early exegetes filled these gaps, producing divergent accounts.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r1.speaker: أهل الرواية والتاريخ
TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r1.claim: Most historians date the story between Jesus and Muḥammad; it is absent from the two Testaments, though some Muslim reports say Quraysh heard it from Jews, while Christians preserved it extensively.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r2.claim: Christian accounts resemble Ibn Isḥāq’s report from Ibn ʿAbbās in some respects but differ from Muslims on the number of sleepers, whether they had a dog, and the length of their sleep.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#38/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#38/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#38/r4.claim: After centuries as a ruined, forgotten site, Jordanian excavation uncovered Rujayb; the author considers its archaeological signs and some Muslim reports the strongest fit for the Qurʾānic cave.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r1.claim: Amman stands on the site of Philadelphia, a major and beautiful city before Islam that remained under Roman control from the early second century until the Muslim conquest.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r2.claim: Other proposed locations include a cave on Mount Qāsiyūn near Damascus, one at Petra, a Scandinavian cave with seven uncorrupted Roman-looking bodies, and a cave near Nakhchivan.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r3.claim: No evidence identifies any proposed cave as the Qurʾānic one; the Scandinavian and Caucasus claims conflict with the story’s Roman setting and the limits of Roman power.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: God alone knows the unseen; others know only what He has disclosed, and claims beyond that knowledge are baseless.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: God's complete knowledge sets up the denial of all deities and intercessors, since none can rival His knowledge or share His authority.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: God alone knows the unseen of heaven and earth; human research has value but cannot rival knowledge conveyed by the Qur'an.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The expressions about God's seeing and hearing intensify praise: nothing escapes Him, so no one can answer better than God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: God's complete knowledge leads into the denial that invented deities or intercessors can help; He shares His authority with no one.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:25/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:25/r1.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:25/r1.claim: In interpretation A, verse 25 reports what people said: some claimed 300 years in the cave and others 309, just as they differed over the youths’ number.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:25/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:25/r3.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:25/r3.claim: On interpretation A, neither their number nor duration is stated by God; verse 26 says only God knows, as the youths themselves said in verse 19.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:25/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:25/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:25/r4.claim: The author prefers interpretation A because the ordering of the verses and their mutually reinforcing indications support it.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:25/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:25/r6.speaker: bir tefsir
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:25/r6.claim: One commentary says the People of the Book also gave 300 years; the extra nine may reconcile their solar-year count with the Arabs’ lunar-year count of 309.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:25/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:25/r7.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:25/r7.claim: On interpretation B, verse 26 settles disagreement by specifying the duration and stressing that God knows it best, since He knows all hidden things and rules without partner.

QIRAAT-ER:18:26:25#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:26:25#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:26:25#1/r1.claim: The second-person jussive reading turns a declaration about divine governance into a prohibition addressed to the Prophet.

STUDYQURAN:18:25/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r1.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r1.claim: Some say the 309 years report the People of the Book’s reckoning, not necessarily the youths’ actual time in the cave; verse 26 then reserves knowledge to God.

STUDYQURAN:18:25/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r10.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r10.claim: In context, God’s statement about the youths and how long they slept may itself be the final judgment on the matter.

STUDYQURAN:18:25/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r2.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r2.claim: Others take 309 years as the youths’ actual sleep in the cave and understand God knows best to concern the interval after their death, shortly after discovery.

STUDYQURAN:18:25/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r3.speaker: still others
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r3.claim: Still others say 309 is the actual duration and settles the dispute about how long they remained.

STUDYQURAN:18:25/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r5.claim: The Unseen belongs to God alone, who alone knows it; the commentary supports this with several verses describing His knowledge of hidden things.

STUDYQURAN:18:25/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r6.claim: The exclamation means that no one sees or hears like God or better than Him, who is the Hearing and the Seeing.

STUDYQURAN:18:25/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r7.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r7.claim: One reported reading takes “they” to mean the youths of the cave, who have no protector except God.

STUDYQURAN:18:25/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r8.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r8.claim: Another reported reading takes “they” to mean those disputing about the youths’ affair, who have no protector except God.

STUDYQURAN:18:25/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r9.claim: God’s judgment is final, with no appeal or revision.

STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r3.claim: The sūrah has three main narratives—the cave youths, Moses and the mysterious servant, and Dhu’l-Qarnayn—and a long parable warning against worldly enjoyment without gratitude and concern for the Hereafter.
